issues.description: The server-side PersonService.savePerson method has a different return type between template and solution and is used inconsistently in the solution. The template declares savePerson as returning Person (public Person savePerson(Person)), and the problem specification/NoteResource pattern imply the service should return the saved Person. In the solution repository PersonService.savePerson was changed to return void, but PersonResource in the solution still calls personService.savePerson(person) and attempts to return its result (ResponseEntity.ok(personService.savePerson(person))). This mismatch makes the solution inconsistent and will not compile, and it conflicts with the expected API behavior described in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the service and resource consistent. Restore PersonService.savePerson to return the saved Person (change its signature back to public Person savePerson(Person person) and return the created/updated Person), so PersonResource can return ResponseEntity.ok(personService.savePerson(person)). Alternatively, if an intentional design change was intended, update PersonResource to not expect a returned Person and adjust the controller to obtain the saved Person (or construct an appropriate response) — but the preferred fix is to match the NoteService pattern and return Person from savePerson.
